description: Composite four-panel figure mixing one mechanical-property plot with three SEM fractographs. (a) is an engineering stress-strain plot, y-axis "Engineering stress/MPa" (0-1000, 200 MPa ticks), x-axis "Engineering strain" (0.0-0.6), with three curves labelled Zr0 (black), Zr0.01 (red) and Zr0.50 (green, Cu-coloured). All peak just above the 800 MPa gridline; the green Zr0.50 curve reaches the highest peak and extends farthest before fracture (between the 0.5 and 0.6 gridlines), the black Zr0 drops first (just past 0.5). An inset shows the true stress-strain curve of Zr0.50 (y-axis "True stress (MPa)" up to 1200; x-axis "True strain" 0.0-0.5; legend "Zr0.50"), with a red dashed horizontal reference line near the 1200 MPa gridline region, which the text identifies as the critical twinning stress ~1.14 GPa. (b)-(d) are SEM fracture surfaces of Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50, each labelled in yellow and bearing a 10 µm scale bar: dimple-dominated surfaces with cleavage facets in (b), dimples becoming larger, deeper and denser toward (d). Together the panels argue that Zr addition raises strength, strain hardening and ductility, consistent with deeper ductile dimples.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots engineering stress (MPa, 0-1000) against engineering strain (0-0.6) for three curves labelled Zr0 (black), Zr0.01 (red) and Zr0.50 (green).

In (a) all three curves peak between the 800 and 1000 MPa gridlines, the green Zr0.50 curve having the highest peak and the black Zr0 curve the lowest, and the curves fracture in the order Zr0 first (just past strain 0.5), then Zr0.01, then Zr0.50 last (near 0.58).

The inset in (a) is a true stress-true strain curve for Zr0.50 (True strain axis 0.0-0.5, True stress axis reaching 1200 MPa) and carries a red dashed horizontal reference line high in the frame, just below the 1200 MPa gridline.
Panels (b)-(d) are secondary-electron SEM fractographs each with a white 10 µm scale bar and a yellow sample label reading Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50 respectively.
The fracture surface in (d) (Zr0.50) shows visibly larger, deeper and more numerous dimples than (b) (Zr0), with pronounced tearing ridges; (c) is intermediate.
The caption states that (b)-(d) are the fracture surfaces of the Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50 steels respectively, and that the inset in (a) is the true stress-strain curve of the Zr0.50 steel.

The citing text reports for Zr0: yield strength ~435 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 820 MPa, fracture ductility 52%; for Zr0.01: ~450 MPa, ~832 MPa, 55%; for Zr0.50: ~505 MPa, ~855 MPa, 58% (values are stated in the text, not printed on the figure).

The citing text states that the critical twinning stress of the Zr0.50 steel is ~1.14 GPa, which is lower than its true ultimate tensile strength shown in the inset of Fig. 4a (the inset's dashed line is the corresponding reference level).

The citing text states that with increasing Zr content the dimples become obviously larger and deeper than in the Zr0 steel and their density also increases, matching the visual trend from (b) to (d).
The citing text describes the Zr0 fracture surface as composed mainly of small dimples and cleavage faces, which is consistent with the small-dimple plus flat-facet morphology visible in (b).

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (y: Engineering stress/MPa 0-1000; x: Engineering strain 0-0.6) for Zr0 (black), Zr0.01 (red) and Zr0.50 (green). Peaks lie between the 800 and 1000 MPa gridlines; Zr0 fractures first and Zr0.50 last, at the largest strain. Inset: true stress-true strain curve of Zr0.50 (True strain 0.0-0.5, True stress up to 1200 MPa) with a red dashed horizontal reference line near the top of the axis.
SEM fracture surface of the Zr0 steel, labelled 'Zr0' in yellow, 10 µm scale bar; small dimples with cleavage faces; top edge slightly cropped.
SEM fracture surface of the Zr0.01 steel, labelled 'Zr0.01' in yellow, 10 µm scale bar; equiaxed dimples that appear somewhat coarser than in (b).
SEM fracture surface of the Zr0.50 steel, labelled 'Zr0.50' in yellow, 10 µm scale bar; the largest and deepest dimples, highest dimple density, with tearing ridges between them.
